_comment: Per-call timeout CEILING (seconds) for every data-fetching / API / collector / renderer / subprocess call in the engine. wp_timeouts.py resolves it — an exported CTI_CALL_TIMEOUT env var first, then CTI_CALL_TIMEOUT= in the skill-root .env (or intel_engine/.env), then this file's call_timeout.value — and exports the result to child processes; wp_common installs a process-wide urllib.request.urlopen floor at that value and every subprocess runner floors its bound to it. NOT applied to raw DNS/TLS/JARM resolution probes (those keep their short fail-fast bounds by design).

call_timeout._comment: value = the ceiling in seconds (5000 ≈ 83 min). Wrapped as a GROUP on purpose: the RULE-3 loader wp_refs.load_ref only surfaces dict/list nodes, so a bare scalar here is silently ignored and the embedded 1800 fallback wins instead.
